title: Time and Work

steps.title: Think in work rates
steps.content: If a person finishes a job in n days, their one-day work rate is 1/n of the job. When people work together, add their rates—not their completion times.
steps.formula:
Rate = 1 ÷ Days
Combined rate = Rate A + Rate B
steps.example: A takes 6 days, B takes 3 days. Together rate = 1/6+1/3 = 1/2 job/day, so they finish in 2 days.

steps.title: Combine two workers
steps.prompt: A finishes a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. How long do they take together?
hints: Convert each worker's completion time into work completed in one day.
Add the rates, not the number of days.

steps.title: Use total work units
steps.content: When times are inconvenient fractions, choose total work as the LCM of individual days. Work/day becomes an integer and the combined time is easier to calculate.
steps.example: A = 12 days, B = 18 days. Take total work = 36 units. A does 3 units/day, B does 2 units/day; together 5 units/day, so time = 36/5 = 7.2 days.
steps.tip: If one worker leaves, subtract their rate from the combined rate.

steps.title: One worker leaves
steps.prompt: A and B together finish a job in 6 days. A alone takes 10 days. How long does B alone take?
hints: Calculate how much work is completed while both workers are present.
Subtract completed work from 1 whole job, then divide by the remaining worker's rate.

steps.title: Work and efficiency
steps.content: For the same job, efficiency is inversely proportional to time. If A is twice as efficient as B, A takes half the time B takes.
steps.example: If B takes 20 days and A is twice as efficient, A takes 10 days.

questions.prompt: A completes a job in 8 days. What fraction of work does A do per day?
A takes 12 days and B takes 12 days. Together they finish in:
A takes 5 days and B takes 20 days. Together they take:
A and B together take 8 days. A alone takes 12 days. B alone takes:
If A is 3 times as efficient as B, and B takes 18 days, A takes:
questions.explanation: Time is inversely proportional to efficiency. A takes 18/3 = 6 days.

learning_objectives: Represent a worker's speed as a fraction of work per unit time.
Relate efficiency ratios to completion times.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Add the number of days to combine workers.
common_misconceptions.correction: Add work rates; completion times are reciprocals of rates.

common_misconceptions.misconception: A faster worker has a larger time per job.
common_misconceptions.correction: A faster worker completes a larger fraction of the job per unit time.

common_misconceptions.misconception: If half the work is complete, half the time always remains.
common_misconceptions.correction: Remaining time depends on the rate of the workers still doing the job.

worked_examples.title: Combine two workers
worked_examples.input: A finishes in 6 days; B finishes in 3 days
worked_examples.explanation: Add rates because both contribute work at the same time.

worked_examples.title: Find one worker's rate
worked_examples.input: A and B finish in 4 days; A alone takes 6 days
worked_examples.explanation: Subtract known rates to isolate the unknown worker's rate.

worked_examples.title: Convert efficiency ratio
trace: For equal time, A completes 2 units.
For equal work, time is inversely proportional to efficiency.
worked_examples.explanation: Higher efficiency means less time for the same amount of work.

company_applications.practice: Convert each completion time to a rate before combining.
Handle a worker leaving by calculating remaining work.
Use a common total-work unit to avoid fraction mistakes.

srs_cards.question: What are the key ideas in Time and Work?
srs_cards.answer: Translate work rates into fractions per unit time. Combine workers' rates correctly. Solve efficiency and alternate-day work problems. Check whether a result is reasonable.

srs_cards.question: Name a common mistake in Time and Work.
srs_cards.answer: Add work rates (work per day), not completion times.

srs_cards.question: How do you find a one-day work rate?
srs_cards.answer: If a worker completes a job in n days, the one-day rate is 1/n of the job.

srs_cards.question: How do two workers' rates combine?
srs_cards.answer: Add their work completed per unit time, then take the reciprocal to find the time for one whole job.

quest.story: A project has multiple workers with different speeds. The academy needs you to calculate how their rates combine and what happens when one worker leaves.
quest.mission: Represent work as rates, combine workers and calculate completion time.
success_criteria: Convert completion time into a one-day work rate.
Add rates for workers working together.
Calculate remaining work after a worker leaves.
